Baltic Exchange Market Report 11 May 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 3001 (23)
Baltic Capesize Index: 4976 (21)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2283 (50)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1527 (5)
Baltic Handysize Index: 838 (5)
CAPESIZE
A relatively subdued yet positive start to the week saw the market edge higher, with gains remaining modest across both basins as participants continued to assess underlying support. The BCI 182 5TC increased marginally by $192 to $45,133, reflecting a market that remained steady rather than particularly aggressive. In the Pacific, sentiment was generally balanced, although activity appeared somewhat restrained with only one miner active on C5 today. Trading levels were reported in the low $15s as the week commenced, with limited concluded business heard through the session before unconfirmed reports emerged late in the day of $15.20 being fixed. Consequently, C5 remained effectively flat, inching up by just 0.015 to $15.215. The Atlantic also experienced a slower start, although sentiment was said to be gradually improving. C3 posted only a marginal gain of $0.105 to $35.614, with bids reportedly circulating around the $34 level against owners seeking closer to $36 on index dates. There was also market discussion of a $35.50 bid for 13-20 June loading, highlighting the current gap between charterer ideas and owner expectations. Meanwhile, bunker markets remained supportive, with Brent crude firming further amid growing concerns that the fragile Middle East ceasefire may unravel, keeping geopolitical risk and supply disruption fears firmly in focus.
PANAMAX
The positive momentum seen last week has carried into the start of this week with the P5TC posting gains of $449 to close at $20,548. In the Atlantic brokers report that owners are holding firm on their trans Alantic offers. This firmness is not necessarily driven by a surge in fresh enquiry but rather by the widening price disparity compared to current levels being achieved on fronthaul trades. Trans Atlantic activity is said to be more balanced, with mineral volumes still lagging behind grains. Market participants have also pointed to a tightening of tonnage availability within the Atlantic basin. Additionally, there is growing discussion around the possibility of some Capesize stems being split, a development that could provide further support to the Panamax market fundamentals. Grain exports from East Coast South America are said to remain active, further reinforcing the positive sentiment and stronger rates being achieved. Messrs British Steel were reported to have covered their Pointe Noire 21/30 May iron ore stem to Immingham on a Swiss Marine vessel at $18.50. Meanwhile, the scrubber fitted CL Daliao (80,876 2020) opening in Rio Grande on 23 May was said to have been fixed for a trans Atlantic trip, although no further details emerged. In the Pacific, sources have emphasised the continued strength of Australian mineral exports which remain a key factor underpinning the rate floor alongside sustained activity from the Indonesian export market. Reported fixtures indicate healthy demand for tonnage although some participants note that the tonnage list is not as tight as in previous weeks. Period interest also remains evident, with several fixtures surfacing today as the overall market outlook continues to hold a positive tone.
SUPRAMAX
It was a rather typical start to the week with no clear direction appearing. The Atlantic was again described as positional with some saying that demand from the US Gulf might be easing. From Asia brokers said that positive sentiment remained in place although again it was a bit early to see if this upward trend in rates would continue. Period action surfaced, the GW Alpha (61,186 2015) CJK 20/22 May was heard fixed at around $19,000 for one years' trading to Chinaland. Also, the Yuan Hai Qing Han (63,776 2025) CJK 16/20 May was linked to Lynux taking a vessel also for 1 year at $19,500. the 11TC started in positive territory, rising $60 to $19,300.

Atlantic
The Summer Queen (64,190 2025) open Egypt was heard to have been placed on subjects at $11,000 delivery Port Said trip Nouakchott with clinker. From last week, the NS Ningbo (64,194 2027) Tampa 11 May was on subjects for US Gulf to Far East grains at $26,500, but no more details came to light. Also, the SSI Prudent (63,868 2022) open New Orleans was on subjects for a trip to the East Mediterranean, some said around $30,000, no more details came to light.

Asia
The Berge Catherine (63,654 2020) open Qingdao was rumoured fixed for a NoPac round redelivery SE Asia in the $19,000s but further details were not disclosed. Also, the Apollonia (63,524 2026) Caofeidian was linked to a backhaul cargo redelivery West Africa (HRA) at $20,000 with steels to Chinaland.

HANDYSIZE
The sector commenced the week on a generally positive note, with a firmer tone prevailing, especially throughout the Asian markets. The BHSI added 5 points to close at 838, while the 7TC average rose $83 to finish at $15,077. Both the Continent and Mediterranean regions experienced a rather subdued trading session. Most participants opted to maintain their positions, leading to limited movement in rates and a quiet overall atmosphere. In the South Atlantic and US Gulf, the market demonstrated continued stability. Available tonnage and cargo demand remained well balanced, contributing to steady activity throughout these regions. Market sentiment in the Pacific was somewhat mixed. Some sources reported consistent and steady activity, while others attributed the observed rise in rates primarily to increasing demand and tighter availability of tonnage. Despite these differing perspectives, the market as a whole retained a firm stance. The Pan Amber (38,220 2012) at Tanjung Langsat was reportedly fixed at $17,000 for multiple legs by Pacific Basin and The Hai Phuong Star (32,139 2008) at Penang was also fixed for multiple legs at $13,500, again by Pacific Basin, but no further details were disclosed for either vessel. The Port Angeles (28,448 2007), open at Samarinda on 18 May, was reportedly fixed for a trip via West Australia to the Philippines, carrying salt, in the $15,000’s by Uming, but further details were not disclosed.

Market Fundamentals
Chinese Crude Steel Production

In the period 20-30 April, crude steel production at Chinese Iron and Steel Association (CISA) member mills fell 3.6% from the preceding ten days to 2.0 Mt/day, the lowest level since March, according to the industry association. However, output stood 7.5% below the same period last year. Meanwhile, Chinese iron ore stockpiles declined for the fifth consecutive week, down 0.3 Mt to 164.3 Mt in the week to 8 May, according to data from 42 portside locations monitored by Umetal.

Trading Commentary
Cape
The Cape FFA curve rallied higher today despite a relatively subdued physical market, with only a $192 increase in the index. The biggest moves were on the front end with May paid up to 40250 and Jun 36500. The May v Jun spread traded sideways at 4000, before closing closer to 3750. The was strong buying towards the end of the day on Jul up to 33500, together pays on the Q3 at 32300. Q4 volumes were good, trading within a range of 31050-31500. Similarly good activity on the Cals today also, with the C27 paid up to 26250 and Cal28 23250 late on.

PMX
PMX finished firmer across the front of the curve today, with the most volatility seen in May and June. May traded 20800–21600 across around 550 lots, while June was the busiest contract, trading 21300–22250 with over 1000 lots, remaining the key interest point. July printed 20900–21600 with August at 20100–20750. September saw a single print at 20000. Q3 traded actively at 20300–20800 around 800 lots, Q4 printed 18200–18600, while Cal 27 remained steady in a tight range of 15200–15350 with more than 700 lots.

SMX + HANDY
A relatively busy start to the week for SMX, as the market was once again well supported and buyers reached for offers pulling the curve up towards contract highs. Positive sentiment in the near term remains, as the May traded up to 18400 (BOM 18972) and Jun traded from 18500 to a high of 19000. Q3 was actively traded from 17850 – 18350, and Q4 16100 – 16350. Cal27 traded 13350 – 13500 and Cal28 at 12200. The Handy market was active, as May traded 15350 – 15400, Jun at 16000, Jul at 15750 and Cal27 traded 12500.

Carbon
After an early sell-off, EU carbon markets rallied steadily to close up 2.6%. The benchmark Dec26 EUA Futures contract was assessed at �77.20/eua, up �1.97 from Friday. The market was bolstered by further indications from the EU that industry support would not necessarily involve an increase in EUA supply. While volumes remained below average, EUA offers tended to be paid throughout the day, with stronger bid activity driving the market higher.

Market Fundamentals
Chinese Crude Steel Production
In the period 20-30 April, crude steel production at Chinese
Iron and Steel Association (CISA) member mills fell 3.6% from
the preceding ten days to 2.0 Mt/day, the lowest level since
March, according to the industry association. However,
output stood 7.5% below the same period last year.
Meanwhile, Chinese iron ore stockpiles declined for the ﬁfth
consecutive week, down 0.3 Mt to 164.3 Mt in the week to 8
May, according to data from 42 portside locations monitored
by Umetal.
Trading Commentary
Cape Routes
The C5 market started the week with another strong day of
gains. June contracts rose to 14.00, while July increased to
13.15, with the June vs July spread trading at 85c. October
also moved higher, trading up to 12.95. In the C3 market,
there was plenty of enquiry, although no trades were
reported.
Cape
The Cape FFA curve rallied higher today despite a relatively
subdued physical market, with only a $192 increase in the
index. The biggest moves were on the front end with May
paid up to 40250 and Jun 36500. The May v Jun spread
traded sideways at 4000, before closing closer to 3750. The
was strong buying towards the end of the day on Jul up to
33500, together pays on the Q3 at 32300. Q4 volumes were
good, trading within a range of 31050-31500. Similarly good
activity on the Cals today also, with the C27 paid up to 26250
and Cal28 23250 late on.
PMX
PMX ﬁnished ﬁrmer across the front of the curve today, with
the most volatility seen in May and June. May traded 20800–
21600 across around 550 lots, while June was the busiest
contract, trading 21300–22250 with over 1000 lots,
remaining the key interest point. July printed 20900–21600
with August at 20100–20750. September saw a single print at
20000. Q3 traded actively at 20300–20800 around 800 lots,
Q4 printed 18200–18600, while Cal 27 remained steady in a
tight range of 15200–15350 with more than 700 lots.
SMX + HANDY
A relatively busy start to the week for SMX, as the market
was once again well supported and buyers reached for oﬀers
pulling the curve up towards contract highs. Positive
sentiment in the near term remains, as the May traded up to
18400 (BOM 18972) and Jun traded from 18500 to a high of
19000. Q3 was actively traded from 17850 – 18350, and Q4
16100 – 16350. Cal27 traded 13350 – 13500 and Cal28 at
12200. The Handy market was active, as May traded 15350 –
15400, Jun at 16000, Jul at 15750 and Cal27 traded 12500.Cape 180 5TC

Meanwhile, Chinese iron ore stockpiles declined for the fifth consecutive week, down 0.3 Mt to 164.3 Mt in the week to 8 May, according to data from 42 portside locations monitored by Umetal.
